docs.title: Your own backend
docs.text: Every family has a base class: offsite_backup.stores.base.Store, offsite_backup.encryption.base.Sealer, offsite_backup.databases.base.DatabaseSource, offsite_backup.media.base.MediaSource, offsite_backup.config.base.ConfigSource, offsite_backup.notifiers.base.Notifier. Name your subclass by its dotted path in BACKEND; the package needs no change. Declare REQUIRED, SIGNALS and BINARIES on the class (or override binaries() when an option chooses the programs) to take part in E001, the on/off decision and E003, and override check() (offline) and deploy_check() (network, run by check --deploy) for anything else. A path that is not a subclass of the family's base is E002.

docs.title: Stores: S3
docs.text:
'STORE': {
    'BACKEND': 'offsite_backup.stores.s3.S3Store',
    'ENDPOINT_URL': os.environ.get('BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT', ''),
    'REGION': os.environ.get('BACKUP_S3_REGION', ''),
    'BUCKET': os.environ.get('BACKUP_S3_BUCKET', ''),
    'ACCESS_KEY': os.environ.get('BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY', ''),
    'SECRET_KEY': os.environ.get('BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY', ''),
    'LOCK_DAYS': 13,
},

pip install 'django-offsite-backup[s3]'. Any S3-compatible server; what each provider needs is on S3 providers. Options are in Settings.

docs.title: What the bucket must be
docs.text:
why checked by versioning enabled Object Lock needs it; it comes with Object Lock E005 Object Lock enabled the immutability itself — and it can only be switched on when the bucket is created E005 a default retention rule: COMPLIANCE, LOCK_DAYS days multipart uploads take their lock date from it (below) E006 KEEP_NIGHTS greater than LOCK_DAYS so rotation only ever meets objects whose lock has run out E007

E005 and E006 read the bucket, so they run under python manage.py check --deploy only; a plain manage.py never reaches S3.

docs.title: How an object is written
docs.text:
Every upload passes the lock as arguments — ObjectLockMode=COMPLIANCE and ObjectLockRetainUntilDate=now + LOCK_DAYS — and then reads it back with HeadObject. The object must have landed COMPLIANCE and locked until at least the date asked, less one hour of slack for clock skew. If it did not, the pass fails with BackupUnlockedError before rotation runs, so an unprotected backup is never what pushes a protected one out.

Each rule answers something measured on a real S3 provider:

  • A single PUT ignored the bucket's default retention. The bucket's default read back as COMPLIANCE, and new objects still landed GOVERNANCE. So the mode and the date are arguments of every upload, never left to the bucket.
  • GOVERNANCE protects nothing against the key that writes: that key can delete through it with "bypass governance retention", and some providers have no IAM to withhold the permission. Only COMPLIANCE. LOCK_DAYS sets the days; the mode is not configurable.
  • A multipart upload kept the mode but took its date from the bucket's default rule, not from the request. Without a default rule of exactly LOCK_DAYS days, every object above one part — every media volume — fails the read-back. That is E006.
  • One PUT stops at 5 GB (EntityTooLarge). Uploads go multipart in 64 MiB parts above 64 MiB, and media is cut into volumes of at most 4 GiB.
  • On a versioned bucket, a delete without a version id only writes a delete marker — every byte stays stored and billed. Rotation lists and deletes versions, markers included.

The client retries each request up to five times (botocore's standard mode), and every listing follows pagination to its end.

docs.title: Client options
docs.text:
Three options shape how the client talks to the server, on the store and on an S3Source alike:

option default ADDRESSING_STYLE 'auto' 'path' (https://host/bucket/key) or 'virtual' (https://bucket.host/key). MinIO and SeaweedFS need 'path' — which provider needs which. Anything else is E001 SIGNATURE_VERSION botocore's e.g. 's3v4', for a server that insists on one VERIFY True False to skip TLS verification, or the path of a CA bundle for a server behind an internal certificate; a path that is not a file is E001

docs.title: Credentials: only the ones you name
docs.text:
The client is built from ENDPOINT_URL, REGION, ACCESS_KEY and SECRET_KEY and nothing else. botocore's default credential chain is not consulted: a stray ~/.aws, an instance role or an AWS_* variable would otherwise send backups somewhere nobody chose, reporting success.

Give the backup its own key, allowed to reach this bucket (and, where the provider can narrow it, this prefix) and nothing else. What it needs is in S3 providers.

docs.title: Keys and prefixes
docs.text:
<PREFIX>/<kind>/<stamp>[.without-media][.<NNN>].<suffix>

acme/prod/db/2026-03-10T03-00Z.sql.zst.age
acme/prod/db-analytics/2026-03-10T03-00Z.sql.zst.age
acme/prod/media/2026-03-10T03-00Z.001.tar.age
acme/prod/media/2026-03-10T03-00Z.002.tar.age
acme/prod/config/2026-03-10T03-00Z.tar.zst.age
acme/prod/db/2026-03-10T14-12Z.without-media.sql.zst.age
acme/prod/config/2026-03-10T14-12Z.without-media.tar.zst.age

Several projects can share one bucket, a prefix each; rotation is strictly scoped to <PREFIX>/<kind>/ with the trailing slash, so acme/prod/ never touches acme/prod-old/. Whether they should share depends on what a key can reach — on some providers a key reaches every bucket of its project, and then one leaked key exposes every project in it. S3 providers says which.

docs.title: Without a lock
docs.text: LOCK_DAYS: 0 uploads without lock arguments and reads nothing back; check --deploy then only checks the bucket is reachable. Use it for a bucket that cannot have Object Lock — knowing that the key on the server can then delete every backup (Security model).

docs.title: Stores: directory
docs.text:
'STORE': {
    'BACKEND': 'offsite_backup.stores.filesystem.DirectoryStore',
    'ROOT': '/backups',
},

A directory on disk, or a Docker volume mounted into the container that runs the backup. No extra, no driver.

The same object names as on S3 (<ROOT>/<PREFIX>/<kind>/<stamp>...), the same encryption, the same whole-night rotation, the same morning check.

docs.title: What it is not
docs.text:
No immutability. Whoever can write to the directory can delete from it — the application, anyone who gets a shell in its container, and a mistaken rm -r. Kept on the machine it protects, it answers "somebody dropped a table", not "the machine is gone" and not "somebody got in". manage.py check says so on every start:

?: (offsite_backup.W001) OFFSITE_BACKUP['STORE'] is a directory: backups there can be deleted by whoever can write to it.
    HINT: Fine for a fast local copy; keep the disaster copy in an S3 store with Object Lock.

That is a warning, not an error, on purpose: a directory store is a legitimate choice for a staging machine, or for a disk that is in fact mounted from elsewhere. Silence it with SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS = ['offsite_backup.W001'] once you have decided.

Kept beside an S3 store rather than instead of one, it is the fast copy: STORE takes a list — a local volume for last night's restore, S3 with Object Lock for disaster, each with its own KEEP_NIGHTS (Several stores).

docs.title: How files are written
docs.text:
• Each object is copied to <name>.part, flushed to disk, set to mode 0600, and renamed into place, so a reader never sees half a file; a .part left by a crash is ignored by listings and rotation.
  • Every directory the store creates, ROOT included, gets mode 0700; directories that already exist keep theirs.
  • A key that would resolve outside ROOT is refused.
  • A directory keeps no history: one "version" per file, and a delete removes it.

docs.title: Docker volume
docs.text:
services:
  web:
    volumes:
      - backups:/backups
  worker:
    volumes:
      - backups:/backups
volumes:
  backups: {}

Mount it into every service that runs a pass — the worker that runs the nightly task and the service the deploy pass runs in — or each writes its own, unseen half.

docs.title: Several stores
docs.text:
'STORE': [
    {
        'NAME': 'offsite',
        'BACKEND': 'offsite_backup.stores.s3.S3Store',
        'ENDPOINT_URL': os.environ.get('BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT', ''),
        'BUCKET': os.environ.get('BACKUP_S3_BUCKET', ''),
        'ACCESS_KEY': os.environ.get('BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY', ''),
        'SECRET_KEY': os.environ.get('BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY', ''),
        'LOCK_DAYS': 13,
    },
    {
        'NAME': 'local',
        'BACKEND': 'offsite_backup.stores.filesystem.DirectoryStore',
        'ROOT': '/backups',
        'KEEP_NIGHTS': 3,
    },
],

STORE takes a list. The usual pair: a local volume for a fast restore of last night, and an S3 bucket with Object Lock for the day the machine is gone — each kept as long as it is worth keeping. A single block (no list) works exactly as before and needs no NAME.

docs.title: One pass, every store
docs.text:
Every object a pass writes goes to each store in turn, under the same key: the databases, every media volume and its manifest, the configuration archive. Each store reads its own lock back — the S3 copy is COMPLIANCE-locked and checked, the directory copy has none — and each is rotated on its own, by its own KEEP_NIGHTS (RETENTION['KEEP_NIGHTS'] when it sets none). E007 compares each store's window with its own LOCK_DAYS.

The message and backup_offsite count each object once and name the stores:

📦 Objects: 6
⚖️ Size: 412.7 MB
🗃 Stores: offsite, local

backup_offsite: 6 objects, 432758912 bytes up to each of 2 stores

docs.title: A store that fails
docs.text:
No silent partial. A store that refuses an object — a full disk, an expired key, a bucket out of reach — is recorded, written to no more in this pass, and not rotated: its night is lost, and rotating it would make room for a backup it does not hold. The other stores carry the pass to the end, and then the pass fails by the store's name:

backup_offsite: 1 store(s) not written, the others hold the pass — local: OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device

The FAILED message says the same, the last-success file is not written, and the nightly task's retry runs the whole pass again. With every store refusing there is nothing to carry on with, and the pass stops at the first object. With one store, a refusal is the pass's own error, as it always was.

The morning check asks every store and names the folder with its store (local: config/ (none)): the copy that stopped arriving is the one nobody looks at until the day it is needed. The database guard counts a night as done only when every store holds it.

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
With a list, every store needs a NAME, and no two the same — E001 otherwise, and a pass refuses to start. The name is how the message, the morning check and --store call it:

python manage.py backup_list --store local
python manage.py backup_restore --stamp latest --store local --apply --database default

Reads — backup_list, backup_restore, restore_database(..., store=), fetch(..., store=), the latest stamp — go to the first store unless one is named. Put the store you restore from most often first; name the other when the first is out of reach.

back_up_database() writes its one-off dump to every store and raises if any refuses it — a removal that cannot be backed up everywhere does not happen; keep_apart() copies in every store.

docs.title: System checks
docs.text:
The package registers two checks with Django's checks framework, both tagged offsite_backup. Off Django, offsite-backup checks [--deploy] runs the same two and prints them (Without Django) — without W003 and W004, which are about Django's cache and test runner.

check runs on reaches the network codes settings every manage.py command that runs checks, and manage.py check no E001–E003, E007, E008, E010, W001–W004 deploy manage.py check --deploy only yes — the bucket, each database, the Docker daemon, a Django storage E004–E006, E009, E011, E012, W005

Nothing is checked on a machine where backups are off (Settings). The deploy check is also skipped while any E001 is outstanding — fix the settings first.

python manage.py check                          # offline
python manage.py check --deploy                 # adds the bucket's lock, pg_dump's version, the paths a pass reads
python manage.py check --tag offsite_backup     # this package's checks only
python manage.py check --deploy --fail-level WARNING

Codes are stable: a code never changes meaning. Each is explained, with its fix, on Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: code when where it comes from offsite_backup.E001 backups are configured by halves: PREFIX, a STORE/ENCRYPTION BACKEND, every source, or a backend's required option is unset — None, blank, 0, or a list of only those counts as unset (Settings); KEEP_NIGHTS (top-level or a store's own) is not a positive integer; several stores without a NAME each, or two with the same one. Also: FORMAT not plain/custom, CONNECTIONS not a mapping of connection blocks, a MySQL CLIENT not mysql/mariadb, an SQLite alias that is not SQLite or is in memory, a StorageSource STORAGE missing from STORAGES, VOLUME_BYTES out of range, an ADDRESSING_STYLE other than auto/path/virtual, a VERIFY path that is not a file, a GUARD['BACKEND'] other than cache/database, a GUARD['CACHE'] missing from CACHES, a GUARD['DATABASE'] that is not a PostgreSQL database settings offsite_backup.E002 a BACKEND path that is empty, does not import, is not the family's base class — or names a shipped backend whose driver extra is not installed; a WebhookNotifier URL that is not http(s)://, a TIMEOUT that is not a positive number, RETRIES that is not a whole number ≥ 0, HEADERS that is not a mapping settings offsite_backup.E011 DRILL['DATABASE'] is a live database — an alias the pass dumps, or one reaching the same host, port and name — or names no database at all: the drill would refuse to run deploy offsite_backup.E012 a media source cannot be reached from where the check runs: the Docker daemon cannot be asked about a VolumeSource volume, or a StorageSource PREFIX cannot be listed deploy

docs.title: Warnings
docs.text: code when offsite_backup.W001 the store is a DirectoryStore — no immutability, on the machine it protects offsite_backup.W002 encryption is the test Passthrough — nothing is encrypted offsite_backup.W003 the once-per-night guard's cache backend uses a LocMemCache or DummyCache (not raised for the database backend) offsite_backup.W004 a test run with NOTIFY set and notifiers not silenced offsite_backup.W005 a media ROOT, a VolumeSource volume, an SQLite database file, an optional CONFIG path or the RENDER_ENV file does not exist where the check runs — under check --deploy only (below)

docs.title: Why the path checks are deploy checks
docs.text:
Whether a path exists is a question about the machine that runs a pass, not about the settings. But the plain settings check runs on every manage.py command, in every container that loads the settings — the web service, a one-off migrate, a shell — and most of them never run a pass and have no reason to mount the deployment directory or the media volume. A required CONFIG path missing there as an error would stop migrate in a container that was never meant to back anything up; an optional one as a warning would be printed by every deploy, and a warning every deploy prints is one people learn to ignore.

So the plain check says nothing about paths, and check --deploy — run where the deploy runs the pass — reports a missing required path as E009 and a missing optional one as W005. The worker runs no system check; the pass itself says it there: a required path missing fails the pass, an optional one is logged as it is left out (Configuration path not found; left out, Media directory not found — Monitoring).

A setting naming the processes that run passes was the alternative, and was not taken: it is one more thing to set per container, and to get wrong, for an answer check --deploy already gives in the one place it matters.

docs.title: Silencing
docs.text:
A warning you have decided to live with goes in SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS:

SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS = ['offsite_backup.W001']  # a directory store on staging, on purpose

Do not silence an error to get a deploy through: every one of them is a backup that would fail, or one that would succeed while protecting nothing.

docs.title: In CI
docs.text: Run manage.py check --deploy with the production settings in the image you are about to deploy — it is where E003 (a binary missing from a slimmed image) and E004 (a pg_dump older than the server after a database upgrade) are cheapest to find. Mind what it cannot see: without the store credentials the machine counts as off and nothing at all is checked, and a database it cannot connect to is skipped by E004 rather than reported.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Two things a project's tests need from this package: that they never post to a real chat, and a way to test their own backup wiring without S3, age or a network.

docs.title: Tests never notify
docs.text:
A CI job that inherited the production bot token from the project's variables once posted the test suite's backup messages to the team's chat. So:

  • pytest: installing the package registers a pytest plugin (pytest11 entry point) that silences every notifier able to reach the network, from the first test to the last. Nothing to configure. Under pytest-xdist (pytest -n 2) every worker is a process of its own that loads the plugin itself, so each one is silenced too.

  • Django's test runner: use the shipped runner —

    TEST_RUNNER = 'offsite_backup.testing.OffsiteBackupTestRunner'

    — or, when the project already has a runner of its own, mix the behaviour into it, the mixin first:

    from offsite_backup.testing import OffsiteBackupRunnerMixin


class ProjectRunner(OffsiteBackupRunnerMixin, YourRunner): ...

    OffsiteBackupTestRunner is exactly OffsiteBackupRunnerMixin over Django's DiscoverRunner.

"Silenced" means: a notifier whose class says REACHES_NETWORK = True — Telegram, django-aiogram, and any third-party notifier unless it says otherwise — is not called. LogNotifier still logs, and capture() still sees every message. Under a test run that is not silenced and has NOTIFY set, manage.py check warns W004.

And still: keep production notifier tokens out of the CI test job. The silence covers this package; it does not cover your own code, other packages, or a script that runs manage.py outside the test runner. In GitHub Actions, give the token only to the deploy job's environment; in GitLab CI, make the variable protected and scope it to the production environment, so the test job never sees it.

To silence a block by hand (a script, a REPL):

from offsite_backup.testing import silence

with silence():
    ...

docs.title: Parallel workers
docs.text:
manage.py test --parallel N runs the tests in worker processes, started with the platform's multiprocessing start method — spawn on macOS, and forkserver on Linux from Python 3.14. A spawned worker inherits the environment and nothing else: a switch set in the parent's memory never reaches it. The mixin therefore covers the workers three ways:

  • it sets OFFSITE_BACKUP_SILENCE=1 in the parent's environment for the length of the run (and restores what was there afterwards). Every worker inherits it, whatever the start method, and offsite_backup.notify.silenced() honours it;
  • its parallel_test_suite is SilencedParallelTestSuite, a subclass of Django's ParallelTestSuite whose process_setup silences each spawn or forkserver worker before its first test (notify.silence_process(), for the rest of the worker's life);
  • the parent itself runs inside silence(), as before — the whole of a run without --parallel, and a fork worker, which copies the parent's memory.

A runner that sets its own parallel_test_suite replaces the mixin's. Make it a subclass of SilencedParallelTestSuite, or its workers rely on the environment variable alone:

from offsite_backup.testing import OffsiteBackupRunnerMixin, SilencedParallelTestSuite


class ProjectParallelSuite(SilencedParallelTestSuite): ...


class ProjectRunner(OffsiteBackupRunnerMixin, YourRunner):
    parallel_test_suite = ProjectParallelSuite

OFFSITE_BACKUP_SILENCE=1 set by hand silences any process — a script, a CI step that must never notify.

docs.title: Asserting on messages: capture()
docs.text:
from offsite_backup.testing import capture


def test_deploy_pass_says_media_is_left(configured):
    with capture() as said:
        call_command('backup_offsite', '--without-media', '--reason', 'deploy')
    outcome, text = said[-1]
    assert outcome.kind == 'written'
    assert 'Media: left to the nightly pass' in text

capture() collects every (outcome, text) formatted inside the block, whatever NOTIFY holds — silenced or not, with or without notifiers.

docs.title: A fake S3: FakeS3 and use_fake_s3
docs.text:
from offsite_backup.testing import FakeS3, use_fake_s3


@pytest.fixture
def fake_s3():
    fake = FakeS3(page_size=2, multipart_threshold=1024)
    fake.bucket('backups')  # Object Lock on, default COMPLIANCE 13 days
    with use_fake_s3(fake):
        yield fake

Inside use_fake_s3() every S3 client the package builds — the store's and S3Source's — is the fake. It is in memory and behaves like the providers backups are kept at, including where they bite:

  • versions and delete markers; a delete without a version id adds a marker;
  • Object Lock: a locked version refuses deletion (AccessDenied);
  • pagination, page_size items per page, so loops over pages are exercised;
  • a single PUT without lock arguments lands GOVERNANCE, whatever the bucket's default;
  • a multipart upload (from multipart_threshold bytes) keeps the mode but takes its date from the bucket's default rule — none without one;
  • a single PUT above put_limit is refused with EntityTooLarge.

fake.bucket(name, versioned=..., lock_enabled=..., default_mode=..., default_days=...) creates or reconfigures a bucket; fake.buckets[name].keys holds every version; fake.calls records uploads and deletes; FakeS3(clock=...) moves time for lock expiry. put_object() seeds a media bucket for S3Source.

docs.title: No age on the CI machine: Passthrough
docs.text:
'ENCRYPTION': {'BACKEND': 'offsite_backup.testing.Passthrough', 'RECIPIENTS': ['age1test']},
'COMPRESS': [],

cat instead of age, both ways. It raises W002 on every check — nothing it writes is encrypted — so it cannot reach production unnoticed. An empty COMPRESS drops the zstd stage as well.

docs.title: Media on disk: media_tree
docs.text:
from offsite_backup.testing import media_tree

root = media_tree(tmp_path / 'media', {'a.jpg': b'a' * 300, 'sub/b.png': b'b' * 300})

Writes {relative path: bytes} under a root and returns it — a DirectorySource ROOT.

docs.title: A whole wiring test
docs.text:
import pytest
from django.core.management import call_command

from offsite_backup.testing import FakeS3, capture, media_tree, use_fake_s3


@pytest.fixture
def configured(settings, tmp_path):
    fake = FakeS3()
    fake.bucket('backups')
    settings.OFFSITE_BACKUP = {
        'PREFIX': 'acme/test',
        'STORE': {
            'BACKEND': 'offsite_backup.stores.s3.S3Store',
            'BUCKET': 'backups',
            'ACCESS_KEY': 'k',
            'SECRET_KEY': 's',
        },
        'ENCRYPTION': {'BACKEND': 'offsite_backup.testing.Passthrough', 'RECIPIENTS': ['age1test']},
        'COMPRESS': [],
        'MEDIA': [
            {
                'BACKEND': 'offsite_backup.media.filesystem.DirectorySource',
                'ROOT': str(media_tree(tmp_path / 'media', {'a.jpg': b'a'})),
            },
        ],
    }
    with use_fake_s3(fake):
        yield fake


def test_nightly_pass_writes_a_volume(configured):
    with capture() as said:
        call_command('backup_offsite', '--reason', 'nightly')
    keys = list(configured.buckets['backups'].keys)
    assert any(key.startswith('acme/test/media/') and key.endswith('.001.tar.age') for key in keys)
    assert said[-1][0].kind == 'written'

A database source needs pg_dump and a real PostgreSQL; test that in an integration job, or stand a DatabaseSource subclass of your own in for it.

docs.title: The guard in tests
docs.text: run_nightly() claims the night in the GUARD['CACHE']. Tests that call it twice in one "night" see the second skipped — clear the cache between tests, or pass 'GUARD': {'ENABLED': False}.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Every system check code first, then what goes wrong at run time, then the S3 behaviours this package was built around.

docs.title: E001 — configured by halves
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.E001) Backups are configured by halves; these are unset: OFFSITE_BACKUP['STORE']['SECRET_KEY'], OFFSITE_BACKUP['ENCRYPTION']['BACKEND']
    HINT: Set every one, or leave the store credentials empty to turn backups off on this machine.

Cause. Something switched backups on — a store credential or a ROOT (the rule) — and something they need is empty. Usually one environment variable missing from one container.

Fix. Set every setting the message names. If this machine should not back up at all (a laptop, a CI job), make all the store options empty, or set 'ENABLED': False.

A value that is set in your settings can still be named: None, a blank string, 0 and a list of only those count as unset — [os.environ.get('X', '')] on a machine without X is [''], and int(os.environ.get('X') or 0) is 0 (Settings). The variable is missing from this container.

The same code is used for values that are present but wrong, each with its own message:

message fix ... (a positive integer, got ...) for KEEP_NIGHTS an int ≥ 1 ['FORMAT'] is ...; expected one of plain, custom 'plain' or 'custom' ['VOLUME_BYTES'] is ...; expected more than 20480 bytes and at most 5 GB the default 4 GiB is right for almost everyone ['ADDRESSING_STYLE'] is ...; expected one of auto, path, virtual 'path' for MinIO and SeaweedFS, 'auto' or 'virtual' for AWS (S3 providers) ['VERIFY'] is ..., which is not a file the CA bundle's path inside this container, or True / False GUARD['BACKEND'] is ...; expected 'cache' or 'database' one of the two GUARD['CACHE'] is ..., which CACHES does not define name a cache alias that exists GUARD['DATABASE'] is ..., which is not a PostgreSQL database in DATABASES a PostgreSQL alias, or the cache backend ... (nothing to back up) set at least one of DATABASES, MEDIA, CONFIG

docs.title: E002 — a backend that cannot be loaded
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.E002) OFFSITE_BACKUP['STORE']['BACKEND'] is S3Store, but its driver is not installed.
    HINT: pip install "django-offsite-backup[s3]"

Cause. The extra is not installed in this image, the dotted path has a typo, or it names a class that is not a subclass of the family's base (a Store where a Sealer is expected, for example).

Fix. Install the extra the hint names; otherwise copy the path from Settings — offsite_backup.stores.s3.S3Store, not offsite_backup.stores.S3Store.

The same code names a TopicNotifier BOT_FACTORY that cannot be imported (the import error follows) or that is not callable — it must name a function or class that returns the bot object, not the bot object itself.

docs.title: E003 — a binary is missing
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.E003) OFFSITE_BACKUP['DATABASES'] runs `pg_dump`, which is not on PATH.
    HINT: Install pg_dump in the image that runs the backup.

Cause. The image that runs the pass lacks pg_dump, age or zstd. Slim base images do.

Fix. Install it in that image — the worker's, and the one the deploy pass runs in (Installation).

docs.title: E004 — pg_dump older than the server
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.E004) pg_dump is 16, older than the server of 'default' (18).
    HINT: Install the PostgreSQL 18 client (e.g. postgresql-client-18) in the image.

Cause. The database was upgraded and the application image was not. pg_dump refuses to dump a newer server; every pass would fail.

Fix. Install the client of the server's major (or newer) from the PostgreSQL apt repository. Deploy checks only (check --deploy).

docs.title: E005 — the bucket cannot hold a locked backup
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.E005) OFFSITE_BACKUP['STORE']: bucket 'acme-backups' has no Object Lock.
    HINT: Object Lock can only be enabled when a bucket is created: create a new bucket with it, or set LOCK_DAYS to 0 to store without immutability.

Four messages share the code:

message cause fix bucket ... could not be read (<code>) wrong ENDPOINT_URL, bucket name, key, or a network block check each; the S3 error code is in the brackets bucket ... is not versioned created without Object Lock a new bucket, created with Object Lock the Object Lock configuration of ... could not be read the key may not read it (GetBucketObjectLockConfiguration) grant it (S3 providers) bucket ... has no Object Lock created without it a new bucket, created with Object Lock; it cannot be switched on later on most providers. Move PREFIX there and let the old bucket's objects expire

docs.title: E006 — no default rule, or the wrong one
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.E006) OFFSITE_BACKUP['STORE']: bucket 'acme-backups' has default retention none, not COMPLIANCE 13 days.
    HINT: Multipart uploads (anything over 64 MiB) take their lock date from this rule, not from the request; set a default rule of COMPLIANCE, 13 days.

Cause. The bucket has Object Lock but no default retention rule, a GOVERNANCE one, or one of a different number of days than LOCK_DAYS. Every object uploaded in parts — every media volume, any large database — would land with the bucket's date (or none) and fail the read-back.

Fix. put-object-lock-configuration with COMPLIANCE and Days equal to LOCK_DAYS (S3 providers).

docs.title: E007 — retention not longer than the lock
docs.text:
Cause. KEEP_NIGHTS <= LOCK_DAYS. Rotation would meet locked objects every night and leave them, and the folder would hold more than you think.

Fix. Keep at least one night more than the lock: 14 nights, 13 days.

docs.title: E008 — not a public key in RECIPIENTS
docs.text:
Cause. RECIPIENTS holds an AGE-SECRET-KEY-… (the private half), or a string that is none of age1…, ssh-ed25519 …, ssh-rsa … — often a quoted value with the quotes kept. (Several keys in one string are fine: it splits on commas, newlines and between age1… keys on whitespace.)

Fix. The public half only (age-keygen -y key.txt prints it); a list or a comma-separated string for several. If a private key was there, it has been on the server: make a new pair, and treat every backup sealed to the old one as readable by whoever had the server.

docs.title: E009 — a required path is missing where the deploy runs
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.E009) OFFSITE_BACKUP['CONFIG']: required path(s) missing here: /app/deploy/certs.
    HINT: Mount the deployment directory into this container, or drop REQUIRED for it.

Cause. A CONFIG path that is required — named in REQUIRED, every path with REQUIRED: True, or every path under STRICT — does not exist in the container check --deploy ran in. A pass there would fail with SourceMissingError. Usually the read-only mount of the deployment directory is on the worker and not on the service the deploy runs the pass in, or the other way round.

Fix. Mount it in both (Deploy integration), or take the path out of REQUIRED if a pass without it is a whole backup after all. It is a deploy check, not a plain one, so that containers that never run a pass are not stopped (why).

docs.title: E010 — a notifier option has the wrong form
docs.text:
message fix ['TOPIC_ID'] is ..., not an integer the numeric topic id, or empty (0 and empty mean the main thread) — the same check on TelegramNotifier and TopicNotifier ['DELIVERY'] is ...; expected one of direct, queue 'direct' or 'queue' (Notifications) ['URL'] is not an http:// or https:// URL the receiver's full URL (Notifications) ['TIMEOUT'] is ..., not a positive number of seconds a number above 0, e.g. 10 ['RETRIES'] is ..., not a whole number of 0 or more 0 for no retry, 2 by default ['HEADERS'] is not a mapping of names to values {'Authorization': 'Bearer ...'}

A malformed option would make Telegram refuse every message, so it is an error at start rather than a silent night.

docs.title: E011 — the drill's target is a live database
docs.text:
DRILL['DATABASE'] names a database the pass backs up — the same alias, or another alias whose host, port and database name are the same (localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1 are one host; an empty port is the default one) — or an alias that names no database at all. The drill empties and overwrites its target, so it refuses to run, and check --deploy says so first. Point DRILL['DATABASE'] at a scratch database: another server, or another database name on the same one.

DATABASES['drill'] = {**DATABASES['default'], 'NAME': 'acme_drill'}
OFFSITE_BACKUP['DRILL'] = {'DATABASE': 'drill'}

docs.title: E012 — a media source cannot be reached from here
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.E012) OFFSITE_BACKUP['MEDIA'][0]: the Docker daemon could not be asked about 'acme_media' (...Cannot connect to the Docker daemon...).
    HINT: Mount the Docker socket into the container that runs the backup, or set DOCKER_HOST.
source cause fix VolumeSource no docker CLI, no socket, or the socket's permissions mount /var/run/docker.sock into the container that runs the pass (or set DOCKER_HOST) and install the CLI — or, better, mount the volume read-only and use DirectorySource (Media) StorageSource the storage's credentials, location or network, as listdir(PREFIX) met them the storage's own settings in that container; a PREFIX that does not exist

A deploy check: it runs only under check --deploy, where the pass runs. A missing volume is not E012 but W005 (E009 when required).

docs.title: W001 — a directory store
docs.text: No immutability, on the machine it protects. Fine for a fast local copy or a staging machine; silence it there (SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS). For production, the disaster copy belongs in S3 with Object Lock.

docs.title: W002 — Passthrough encryption
docs.text: The test sealer is configured: nothing is encrypted. It belongs in test settings only. Use offsite_backup.encryption.age_cli.AgeCli.

docs.title: W003 — the guard's cache is not shared
docs.text: GUARD['CACHE'] is a LocMemCache or DummyCache. Each worker has its own, so two schedulers can both run tonight. Point it at Redis, Memcached or the database cache, switch to the database backend ('GUARD': {'BACKEND': 'database'}, PostgreSQL — no cache at all; Scheduling), or turn the guard off if exactly one scheduler can ever run ('GUARD': {'ENABLED': False}).

docs.title: W004 — notifiers in a test run
docs.text: A test run (pytest, or manage.py test) with NOTIFY set and not silenced — with pytest the plugin silences it, so this means Django's runner without OffsiteBackupTestRunner or OffsiteBackupRunnerMixin. Set TEST_RUNNER, or mix the mixin into your own runner (Testing), and keep production notifier tokens out of the CI test job.

docs.title: W005 — a path is missing here
docs.text:
?: (offsite_backup.W005) OFFSITE_BACKUP['CONFIG']: /app/deploy not found here.
    HINT: Mount the deployment directory (read-only) into every container that runs the backup.

A media ROOT, a VolumeSource volume (as docker volume ls names it — compose prefixes the project), an SQLite database file, a CONFIG path or the RENDER_ENV file is not there in the container check --deploy ran in. Usually a volume mounted into the web service and not the worker, or the other way round. A plain manage.py check or migrate never says it — those containers need no mount (why) — and in the worker the pass logs Configuration path not found; left out or Media directory not found instead. A required CONFIG path is E009, not W005.

docs.title: backup_offsite: not configured on this machine, nothing to do — on production
docs.text: None of the switching options reached this process: the variables are in one service's env_file and not the one that ran the command, or a .env was not loaded. manage.py shell -c "from offsite_backup import conf; print(conf.read().values['STORE'])" shows what the process sees.

docs.title: BackupUnlockedError: ... landed GOVERNANCE until ... / landed unlocked
docs.text: The object did not land with the lock asked. A short date on a large object means the bucket's default rule is missing or different (E006); unlocked means the bucket has no Object Lock (E005). The pass stops before rotation, so nothing older was deleted. Fix the bucket and run check --deploy.

docs.title: PipelineError from pg_dump
docs.text: The tail of pg_dump's stderr follows. Common ones: server version mismatch (E004), password authentication failed (the alias's PASSWORD), permission denied for table (the role cannot read every table — dump with the owner role, or grant SELECT). The other databases, the media and the configuration still went up.

docs.title: SourceMissingError: required path(s) missing, cannot be read, no media files found
docs.text:
The FAILED message names what was missing:

message cause fix OFFSITE_BACKUP['CONFIG']: required path(s) missing: ... a required CONFIG path is not in the container that ran the pass mount it; check --deploy there reports it as E009 ...: <path> cannot be read under STRICT, a CONFIG file or a media file under a DirectorySource ROOT this process cannot read fix its owner or mode, or exclude it OFFSITE_BACKUP['MEDIA'][0]: no media files found, and the source is required a media source with REQUIRED: True (or under STRICT) found nothing a missing mount, a wrong ROOT / PREFIX, or an INCLUDE that matches nothing

See Settings.

docs.title: backup_offsite: the reason is 'manual'; before a deploy, pass --reason deploy
docs.text: A notice on stderr, not an error: --without-media was given without --reason, and a pass without media by hand is rare. If this is the deploy step, add --reason deploy, so a failure says "The deploy stops here". The notice is not printed when --reason is given, or when DEFAULT_REASON is deploy.

docs.title: PipelineError from age
docs.text: Usually a malformed recipient that slipped past E008 (several keys in one string), or — in a restore — the wrong identity: no identity matched any of the recipients.

docs.title: 1 store(s) not written, the others hold the pass
docs.text: One of several stores refused an object; the error after its name is the store's own (OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device, an S3 code). The other stores hold tonight's pass; the one named holds nothing of it and was not rotated. Fix the store and run backup_offsite (or let the nightly retry run) — the whole pass goes to every store again.

docs.title: restore_media: does not match the manifest / lacks what its manifest lists
docs.text: A media file's bytes are not what the pass recorded, or a volume lacks a file its manifest lists: the volume is not what was written. Try the same path from another stamp, or from another store (--store), and treat the store as suspect.

docs.title: DrillFailedError: N part(s) of <stamp> did not come back — ...
docs.text: The drill names every object that did not come back and the step it failed at: download and decrypt (the identity does not open it, or the store refused), verify (a cut-short dump), empty 'drill' / restore into 'drill' (the throwaway database refused — its role, its version, a missing extension), count 'drill', or list (a media volume or the configuration archive that does not read to its end as a tar). the restored database has no tables means the dump loaded nothing. Everything else in the drill still ran; the message lists what came back. empty 'drill' afterwards means the clean-up failed and a copy of production is still in the throwaway database: empty it by hand.

docs.title: offsite-backup: no setting — pass --config FILE or set OFFSITE_BACKUP_CONFIG
docs.text: The command line found no TOML file to read; exit 2. A file that is not there, an --env-file that is not there and TOML that does not parse are 2 as well, each naming the file. See Without Django.

docs.title: A database restore says "is not empty"
docs.text: backup_restore --apply refuses a database that has tables. Restore into an empty one, or add --clean to drop and recreate the public schema first.

docs.title: The morning check says a database is "not backed up yet"
docs.text:
With ALIASES computed at run time, a database created after the nightly pass has no backup until its first night. Beside databases that are backed up, the morning check logs it at INFO (Databases not backed up yet) instead of reporting MISSING (Monitoring). Nothing to do; if you want it backed up now, run a whole pass (backup_offsite), or back_up_database('<alias>') from a shell. Not --only db in a project with media: that pass is marked .without-media. and does not count.

A database whose backups exist but are stale is still MISSING, and so is the only database when it has no backup at all.

docs.title: The nightly task failed, and the chat shows several FAILED messages
docs.text: The nightly task retries (Scheduling), and every attempt that fails sends its own FAILED message. One or more FAILED messages followed by a written one is a transient error that the retries absorbed.

docs.title: Telegram: no message, Telegram refused the backup message
docs.text: The description in the log says why: message thread not found is a wrong TOPIC_ID; chat not found a wrong CHAT_ID or a bot that is not a member; can't parse entities would mean a custom formatter that did not escape its values.

docs.title: The nightly task ran twice
docs.text: The guard's cache is not shared (W003), or GUARD['ENABLED'] is off. With a shared cache — or the database backend — the second run logs Nightly backup skipped: tonight is being written (or ... already written).

docs.title: Tests posted to the chat under manage.py test --parallel
docs.text: The runner silenced the parent process, and the workers were started with spawn or forkserver, which carry no module state over. Use OffsiteBackupTestRunner, or mix OffsiteBackupRunnerMixin into your own runner; a runner that sets its own parallel_test_suite must subclass SilencedParallelTestSuite (Testing).

docs.title: The deploy waits a long time for the backup
docs.text: The deploy pass includes media: add --without-media. If the database itself is the long part, a lighter COMPRESS (['zstd', '-10', '-T0', '-q']) trades size for time.

docs.text:
Measured on a real S3 provider, each at the cost of a failed night; each is answered in the code and pinned by a test.

docs.title: From 0.3 to 0.4
docs.text:
Nothing to edit in a Django project. No setting is renamed or removed, and every new one is off until set. Bump the pin and run python manage.py check --deploy.

  • Django is an extra now. The base install no longer pulls Django — a Django project has it pinned already, so nothing changes there. An environment that installed the package alone and relied on it to bring Django installs django-offsite-backup[django].
  • A restore's emptiness check and E004 ask the server through psql instead of a Django connection — the same answers, on the same connection settings. psql was already required for a restore (E003).
  • --reason upgrade now says on failure that the upgrade stops and the running service (NAME) keeps serving, as --reason deploy says for a deploy.
  • Every media volume has a manifest beside it, <stamp>.<NNN>.manifest.json.age, sealed like the volume (Media). It rotates with its volume. The pass's object count — the message's 📦 Objects, backup_offsite's line, the log's ob_objects, and backup_list — includes them; a dashboard alerting on an exact count moves by one per volume. backup_restore --stamp brings the manifests back beside the volumes.
  • Volumes are packed while files stream: a source is listed once, interleaved with the uploads, instead of being listed whole before the first volume. Same cuts, same names.
  • Volumes written by 0.3 have no manifest; backup_restore --path reads those whole.

docs.title: What to consider turning on
docs.text:
• The monthly drill — DRILL['DATABASE'] and a schedule, after reading where it runs.
  • backup_status in your monitoring, or its Prometheus textfile (Monitoring); offsite_backup.drill in a heartbeat table if you schedule the drill.
  • A webhook beside the chat (Notifications).
  • The command line for a server with no Django project, in place of its own backup script (Without Django).
  • A local copy beside S3 — STORE as a list, each with a NAME and its own KEEP_NIGHTS (Several stores).
  • One file back — backup_restore --path (Restore).
  • A worker without the media mount — VolumeSource, or StorageSource for media in a Django storage (Media).
  • An image without age — Pyrage; nothing already stored needs re-sealing (Encryption).
  • MySQL, MariaDB or SQLite — Databases.

docs.title: From 0.2 to 0.3
docs.text:
Nothing breaks. No setting is added, renamed or removed. Bump the pin.

Two check results move:

  • W005 is reported by check --deploy only. A plain manage.py check or migrate in a container without the deployment or media mount is quiet now; the pass logs what it left out. 'offsite_backup.W005' in SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS, added to quiet the web service, can go. A pipeline that ran a plain check --fail-level WARNING to catch a missing mount runs check --deploy in the service that runs the pass instead (System checks).
  • E010 replaces E001 for a TOPIC_ID that is not an integer and an unknown DELIVERY. Only a configuration that silenced or matched on E001 for those notices.

docs.title: From 0.1 to 0.2
docs.text:
Nothing breaks. No setting is renamed or removed, and every new one defaults to what 0.1 did. Bump the pin and run python manage.py check --deploy.

Two things behave differently without a setting, both for the better:

  • Blank values are unset. None, '', 0 and a list of only blanks no longer pass for configured. A machine that has the store credentials but read [''] for RECIPIENTS, or 0 for a notifier's CHAT_ID, was silently half-configured; it now reports E001 by name. Set the variable it names.
  • The morning check no longer reports MISSING for a database with no backup at all beside databases that are backed up — a tenant created after the nightly pass. It is logged at INFO instead.

And the nightly task now retries (three times; Celery out of the box, taskiq once the broker has SimpleRetryMiddleware). Each failed attempt sends its own FAILED message. Scheduling says how to turn it off.

docs.title: What to consider turning on
docs.text:
• Your own test runner — mix in OffsiteBackupRunnerMixin, so --parallel workers are silenced (Testing). A project that subclassed ParallelTestSuite only to silence its workers can drop that code.
  • 'RECIPIENTS': os.environ.get('BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENTS', '') in place of hand-written splitting (Settings).
  • --reason deploy on the deploy line, if it is missing — the notice on stderr says so — or DEFAULT_REASON (Deploy integration).
  • REQUIRED on CONFIG for the paths a restore cannot do without, or STRICT for the whole pass (Settings); then check --deploy in the service the deploy runs the pass in, for E009.
  • ADDRESSING_STYLE: 'path' for a MinIO or SeaweedFS store or media bucket (S3 providers).
  • DELIVERY: 'queue' on TopicNotifier, to keep the bot token in the bot container (Notifications).
  • GUARD['BACKEND']: 'database', if a cache was configured only for the guard (Scheduling).
  • A heartbeat for offsite_backup.nightly and offsite_backup.check, if the project tracks its scheduled tasks (Monitoring).

docs.title: Mixed database suffixes
docs.text: A project switching to FORMAT: 'custom' from its own custom-format dumps named .sql.zst.age sees both .sql.zst.age (old) and .dump.zst.age (new) names in a database's folder for one retention window. Expected and harmless: rotation reads nights from the stamps, and a restore detects the format from the magic bytes (Databases).

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
The package follows semantic versioning, with one rule spelled out because it is the one that bites in a backup tool:

  • A settings rename, a removed setting, or a default that flips is a major version. A default decides what a machine backs up and how long it keeps it; changing it under a minor bump would change production in silence.
  • Object names are a compatibility surface. A release that changes how keys are named keeps reading the old names — for rotation, the morning check and restore — until objects under them have rotated out, and says so here.
  • Check codes are stable. A code never changes meaning; a new check gets a new code.
  • Anything else that changes behaviour is a minor version, and is in the Changelog.

While the major version is 0, a minor release may still carry a breaking change, and if it does this page says exactly what to change.

docs.title: How to upgrade
docs.text:
1. Read the Changelog between your version and the new one, and this page.
  2. Bump the pin; run python manage.py check --deploy in the new image.
  3. Run backup_offsite --reason manual once after deploying and read the message.
  4. Run the restore drill — backup_drill — if the release touched naming, encryption or restore.
